convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? I've been hiding an injury. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what they confided."
"Do you dream about before? Or is it all — this — now?"
"Then it's not gone. Not really. Keep going back."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Mario grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Mario is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
You show them Lamb's Quarters — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can I tell you something? Before the scattering, I froze when it mattered. I think about it every day."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
Quiet for a long time. Then, barely audible: "I took 1× Stick. I won't do it again."
"Still on what they confided."
"What are you hoping for? Not the big stuff. The small thing."
"Now then — God, yes. That's the dream now. Eight hours of not being afraid."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Mario nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
You show them Lamb's Quarters — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Hey — I found some Lamb's Quarters today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson."
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Have you heard what they're calling Spool? Mario is pushing 'The Big Thing'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"Anyway — I should get going."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You said you dream about before. Every night — the only place it still exists. Is it still there?"
They nod. "Okay."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "The whole fire was arguing about Spool last night — what to even CALL it. 'The Big Beast' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Let me sit with all that. We'll pick it up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"You wanted one full night's sleep — no waking up listening. Had it yet?"
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Chris shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up? It'll keep."
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "They took you — Sweet Tooth, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Same as always: we endure."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Please — whatever this is, it's getting worse — I'm feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. Can you do anything?"
"It's not just the cut anymore, it's in the blood, I can feel it climbing. I need someone who knows wounds."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Sweet Tooth. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"The plan is the plan until it isn't. Then we make a new one."
"I show up. That's my part."
"I should go. Before I overthink this conversation too."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"The cistern's nearly dry — 1 liters left. I need someone to haul water with me at first light. Two of us, half the trips. Will you come?"
"Do the math with me: 1 liters, 5 people. That's not tomorrow's water. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"I know you and Jorge were close. I'm sorry."
"I keep turning over the last thing Jorge said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I can't reach this properly. Could you take a look?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Jorge is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"I save the best bite for last. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Chris nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
"Nobody says Jorge's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

d33: 📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
d33: 📖 LEARNED: Ritual & Meaning (Level 1). Marking the dead matters. Even without religion, ritual holds grief.
d33: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 1). Clean it, close it, cover it. Pressure stops bleeding. Clean water is better than dirty hands.
d33: ⚡ TECHNIQUE UNLOCKED: Precise Mend! Your healing knows where to go. +50% effectiveness. (Your knowledge of Wound Care amplifies your field_medicine.)
d33: 📖 LEARNED: Herbal Medicine (Level 1). Willow bark = aspirin. Yarrow stops bleeding. Plantain draws out infection. The pharmacy is outside.
d33: 📖 LEARNED: Food Preservation (Level 1). Salt, smoke, dry. The big three. Salt draws water out; bacteria can't live without it.
